limitations: This is a development-validation report, not final held-out test performance. No new model inference or final-test evaluation was performed by this reviewer.
Three policy seeds and eight fixed validation mazes provide limited evidence; 24 episodes do not mean 24 distinct mazes.
Validation was repeatedly observed and used to select C/D reference settings, so provisional selection can overfit this small development set.
Reported variability is sample standard deviation across policy seeds, not a confidence interval or uncertainty across maze distributions.
Training return includes epsilon-greedy exploration; final training-maze and validation success use greedy policies and are different metrics.
Episode counts differ between seeds because successful episodes terminate early. Cross-condition sample-efficiency comparison must use environment steps as well.
Path efficiency is conditional on successful episodes; values of 1.0 do not indicate every evaluation maze was solved.
Exact causes of failure or poor generalization remain hypotheses. Zero seed dispersion with universal failure is not evidence of useful stability.
Wall-clock timings were observed under a varying desktop workload and are not a controlled hardware-speed benchmark.
Storage retry changed execution plumbing; recovered B combines exact completed artifacts from the original code commit with one seed restarted after the storage-only fix. Provenance is retained.
approved_claims: In this fixed 10x10 development experiment, increasing the training budget from 2000 to 20000 steps changed final mean validation success from 0% to 4.1667%.
At the same 20000-step budget, longer exploration produced final validation success of 12.5% mean with 21.6506 percentage-point sample SD across seeds [0%,37.5%,0%].
Lowering learning rate to 0.0003 under the selected exploration condition produced 0% final validation success in this run.
Increasing FC width from 64 to 128 increased parameters from 210212 to 415332 and produced 4.1667% mean validation success, versus 12.5% for its B reference.
The provisionally selected B condition had 54.1667% mean greedy success on familiar training mazes and 12.5% on the fixed validation mazes.
All claims compare the latest checkpoints. The final held-out test set was not used by the study code or recorded evaluation workflow.
unapproved_claims: A larger model generally worsens DQN or longer exploration generally solves mazes.
Exploration is proven to be the sole cause of failure, or the familiar/unseen gap proves one specific overfitting mechanism.
These results establish final generalization performance, statistical significance, or algorithm superiority.
Reward growth alone proves successful navigation, or a single best intermediate result is the final success rate.
All 24 evaluation episodes are independent maze instances, or a zero standard deviation from all failures means robust success.
evidence_basis: Independent recomputation of stored artifacts and CPU checkpoint metadata; no retraining or model evaluation.
